field.label: Sub-tick release (beta)
field.help: Shape with dummynet-st: dummynet with CAKE built in, which releases packets between clock ticks rather than a tick's worth at a time, so they wait less and leave in smaller bursts. Off: the stock dummynet and dn_cake.ko. The stock dummynet is used anyway when dummynet-st does not match the kernel, and, until Try dummynet-st again (shown above when it applies), after a panic while it was in use, or two boots in a row that ended without a clean shutdown (power cuts, resets or hangs). Beta, on by default: to stay on the stock dummynet, untick this and Apply.

field.label: Sub-tick release for
field.help: Pipes with CAKE: dummynet-st is loaded while a CAKE entry is enabled. All pipes: also when the shaper has pipes but no CAKE entry, so that pipes with FQ-CoDel, FQ-PIE or another scheduler release between ticks too, and their CoDel or PIE measures delay with the precise clock. Either way, once it is loaded every pipe releases this way.

field.label: Release interval (us)
field.help: The longest a packet waits for release once the pipe's rate lets it go, in microseconds. Lower releases more often, at more CPU cost on a router short of it; the clock tick (1000 at kern.hz=1000) or more releases once per tick, as the stock dummynet. Applies to every shaper pipe, not only the CAKE ones.

field.label: Skip ipfw on output for traffic shaped inbound
field.help: With dummynet-st, a packet a shaper rule on "in" queued is sent on without passing the traffic shaper's rules (ipfw) a second time on its way out, where they would pass it anyway. Saves CPU on small firewalls: about a tenth of a CPU at 200 Mbit/s each way on an Atom. Takes effect only while every enabled shaper rule is an "in" rule on a single interface and no captive portal zone exists, as no ipfw rule then applies to that traffic on output; otherwise this page says why it is not in effect. Set up a captive portal later and this page warns until Apply turns it off.
